shape.subjectTooLong: Subject is {len} characters; the limit is {max}. Put detail in the work-graph node or the lesson catalog.
shape.bodyTooManyLines: Body has {n} prose lines; the limit is {max} (structured lines and trailers are not counted).
shape.bodyTooLong: Body prose is {n} characters; the limit is {max}.
shape.structuredTooLong: "{prefix}" line is {n} characters; the limit is {max}.
shape.roundsNotInteger: "{line}" must be a whole number, got "{value}".
shape.thirdRoundMissing: {rounds} review rounds exceed the limit of {max}; add "{line} <signal> — <reason>" naming the independent signal (test, mutation run, real measurement) that justified it.
shape.impactMissing: Staged paths need an impact table ({paths}); add a "{line}" line that holds the summary on that same line, or "{line} not needed — <reason>".
shape.cochange: Warning: {paths} changed, but not {docs}{note}. If the change shows there, update it in this commit.
shape.forbidden: {where} adds "{text}", which review.forbidden rule {rule} keeps out{note}. Take it out; naming the file in that rule's except list is for the user to decide.
shape.forbiddenMerged: The merge brings {n} of these lines from {commit}: fix them on that branch, then merge again.
shape.forbiddenUnread: review.forbidden rule {rule} ("{text}") was not checked in {where}: those lines are not UTF-8, and a text with letters outside ASCII has no single spelling there.
shape.forbiddenBinaryUnread: review.forbidden rule {rule} ("{text}") was not checked in {n} file(s) with NULs (binary, UTF-16 or UTF-32) for its spellings in 8-bit encodings.
shape.forbiddenWideUnread: review.forbidden rule {rule} ("{text}") was not checked in {where} as UTF-16 or UTF-32 text: {reason}.
shape.secret: {where} adds what reads as a secret. Take it out, and if it is real revoke it where it was issued: it has been written to disk. Whether a file may hold one (a test fixture) under security.secrets.except is for the user to decide.
cli.secretsUnmeasured: security.secrets was not checked: the staged lines could not be read ({error}).
cli.secretsPastBudget: security.secrets was not checked in {n} staged path(s) ({paths}): the lines they add are past the {mb} MB the hook reads of a commit, the smallest files first.
cli.secretsReadFailed: security.secrets was not checked in {n} staged path(s) ({paths}): {error}; the other staged files were.
cli.secretsUnseen: security.secrets was not checked in {n} staged path(s) git's diff did not show ({paths}).
cli.secretsKeyUnread: security.secrets was not checked for a private key around the added lines of {n} staged file(s) ({paths}): {reason}.
cli.configUnstaged: Warning: {path} in the work tree is not what this commit holds; every check used the commit's own config.
cli.configUnstagedUnread: Warning: {path} in the work tree could not be read or does not load; every check used the commit's own config.
cli.configUnmeasured: The commit's own config could not be read ({error}); the work tree's was used, and what this commit loosens was not read.
cli.configDeletedUnread: The files this commit deletes could not be read ({error}), so what it loosens was not compared with a config among them.
cli.configNotInCommit: {path} is in no commit, so what it loosens cannot be read; the checks used it as it stands. Committed, it is compared on every commit.
cli.configNamedIgnored: ENNYN_CONFIG names {named}; the checks used the commit's own {path}.
cli.configHeadUnread: {path} as HEAD holds it could not be read or does not load ({error}), so what this commit loosens was not read.
cli.configCommitBroken: {path} as this commit holds it does not load ({error}): from here on no check would run. HEAD's rules were used.
cli.configCommitUnread: {path} as this commit holds it could not be read ({error}); HEAD's rules were used, and what it loosens was not read.
shape.loosening: This commit loosens {keys}, so a gate would let through what it refuses now. Loosening a gate is the user's call, not the agent's: ask them, and only on their plain yes for each key add the body line "{line} <key>, <key>".
shape.looseningNoComment: This commit loosens {keys}, and git's comment marker could not be read ({error}), so a line {line} may not be stored and counts for nothing. Commit again when git answers; loosening a gate stays the user's call.
shape.looseningWord: A line {line} counted for nothing: {word} is no key this commit loosens or that a config holds. After the colon a line holds keys, spaces, tabs and commas alone.
shape.looseningFixup: This fixup! commit loosens {keys}, and git drops a fixup!'s message when it folds it, so the approval would leave no record. Use --fixup=amend: or a commit of its own.
shape.allowNoReason: "{marker}" needs a reason of at least 8 characters before the closing bracket.
sidecopy.header: Rules that apply to the file {relPath} in the project, given here because you are working in a side copy of it:
sidecopy.tooLarge: Rules that apply to the file {relPath} in the project (too large to inline; read them with the Read tool):
sidecopy.changed: this text replaces the one given before
doctor.injectAboveCap: sideCopy.maxInjectBytes is {n}, above the 10,000 characters Claude Code keeps of a hook's added context; 10,000 is used
sidecopy.listMore: …and {n} more rule files that apply here
push.warn: {n} commits are waiting to be pushed (threshold {max}). Ask for push approval; large batches hide which change broke what.
push.unmeasured: Unpushed commit count could not be measured (no upstream branch).
push.ok: {n} commits are waiting to be pushed (threshold {max}).

cli.forbiddenUnmeasured: review.forbidden was not checked: the staged lines could not be read ({error}).
cli.forbiddenReadFailed: review.forbidden was not checked in {n} staged path(s) ({paths}): {error}; the other staged files were.
cli.forbiddenNamesUnread: review.forbidden was not checked in {n} staged path(s) whose names are not UTF-8 ({paths}): git cannot be asked for them by name, so this commit is refused. Give them UTF-8 names, or leave them out of this commit.
cli.ciNamesUnread: security.ci was not checked in {n} staged path(s) whose names are not UTF-8 ({paths}): git cannot be asked for them by name, so this commit is refused. Give them UTF-8 names, or leave them out of this commit.
cli.ciTrackedUnread: security.ci was not checked in {n} tracked CI file(s) whose names are not UTF-8 ({paths}): git cannot be asked for them by name; what they hold for this commit is not known.
cli.ciCallersUnread: security.ci could not read the workflows that may call the staged files ({error}); what they reach was not checked, the staged files were checked on their own.
cli.ciCalleesUnread: security.ci could not read the local callees {paths} ({error}); what they check out was not checked.
cli.ciUnmeasured: security.ci was not checked: the staged CI files could not be read ({error}).
cli.ciCalleesNoName: no git argument can hold that name
cli.gateRefused: {gate} was not checked, so this commit is refused: {what} could not be read ({error}). The commit's own content can cause this failure, and so can a bug in Ennyn; only a fault of the machine lets a commit through. Change what is named, or leave it out of this commit; if neither helps, report it as a bug in Ennyn.
cli.ciFilesUnread: security.ci could not read {paths} ({error}); what they hold was not checked, the other CI files were.
cli.depsFilesUnread: security.deps could not read {paths} ({error}); what they hold was not checked, the other files were.
cli.stagedDeletedUnread: The list of staged paths is past {mb} MB: this check could not name what this commit deletes, and read what it adds or changes.
ci.unpinned: {path}: {n} new uses name code that can change under the same name (a tag, a branch, a local path inside a checkout by branch): line {where}; name the full commit SHA (owner/repo@<40 hex> # v1.2.3)
ci.pwn: {path}: a pull_request_target workflow checks out the pull request's code, which then runs with this repository's secrets and a write token: line {where}
ci.permissions: {path}: neither the workflow nor these jobs set permissions, so they get the repository's default token, which may write: line {where}; add `permissions: contents: read` at the top
ci.writeAll: {path}: permissions: write-all gives every scope: line {where}
ci.unread: {path}: not checked ({reason}); its uses, triggers and permissions are not known
ci.unreadNew: {path}: this commit brings a file the check cannot read ({reason}), and the runner may still run it: its uses, triggers and permissions are not known; make it a plain UTF-8 file of at most 16 MB
ci.forms: {path}: YAML the check cannot follow, which GitHub may still run: line {where}; write it plainly
ci.calleeUnread: {path}: a pull_request_target workflow reaches {callee} at line {n}, which the check does not read; what it checks out was not checked
ci.reason.notBlob: not a blob git can read
ci.reason.notFound: not in the index or HEAD under this name
cli.depsNamesUnread: security.deps was not checked in {n} staged path(s) whose names are not UTF-8 ({paths}): git cannot be asked for them by name, so this commit is refused. Give them UTF-8 names, or leave them out of this commit.
cli.depsUnmeasured: security.deps was not checked: the staged lock files could not be read ({error}).

deps.pkgUnreadStill: {path} was not checked against {where}, which the check cannot read
deps.overrideNotLifted: {path}: an override in package.json does not lift these refusals ({where}): the check judges every spec npm may read, an overridden one too
deps.baselineUnread: {path} was not checked: HEAD's version could not be read ({reason}), so what this commit brings is unknown

deps.mismatch: {path}: {n} new entries name one package and install another (npm installs the tarball resolved names): {where}
deps.integrity: {path}: {n} new entries have no integrity, so npm installs whatever the registry sends: {where}
deps.integrityWeak: {path}: {n} new entries are sealed by no sha512 integrity, only a weaker one: {where}
deps.tampered: {path}: {n} new entries hold an integrity that is not the registry's for that version: {where}
deps.hiddenScripts: {path}: {n} new entries run install scripts by their registry manifest, which the lock leaves out: {where}; listing each one trusted in security.deps.allowScripts is for the user to decide
deps.young: {path}: {n} new versions are younger than {days} days, too new for anyone to have looked at them: {where}; wait; listing name@version in security.deps.allow is for the user to decide

deps.unread: {path}: age, adoption, the registry's integrity and install scripts unmeasured for {n} new versions ({reason}): {where}

deps.npmrcSaid: {path}: where npm fetches from is unmeasured ({why}): line {where}
deps.npmrcIndirect: {path}: makes npm read another config file, which the check does not read: line {where}; a project's .npmrc has no use for it
deps.reason.offlineCache: a cache npm installs from offline
deps.noneMeasured: {path} has dependencies, and no lock file beside it or above it: what npm installs there is unmeasured
deps.untracked: {path} is read, but not tracked: what is installed is not what is committed
deps.mismatchEntry: {where} names one package and installs another: {reason}
deps.scriptEntry: {where} runs install scripts; listing it in security.deps.allowScripts is for the user to decide
deps.summary: lock files: {files} · entries: {entries} · advisories: {advisories} · install scripts: {scripts} · refused: {refused} · unmeasured: {unchecked}

deps.reason.badUrl: a resolved URL that does not parse
deps.reason.unlisted: from {from}, which security.deps.registries does not list
deps.reason.timeout: no answer within the {s} s budget
deps.reason.notFound: not found (a private package, or none of that name)

deps.reason.noSuchVersion: the registry has no such version

deps.reason.noDownloads: an answer with no downloads per version

deps.reason.countMismatch: an answer with another number of results than queries

deps.reason.notBlob: not a blob git can read
deps.unreadAge: {path}: age and adoption unmeasured for {n} new versions ({reason}): {where}
deps.v1: {path}: lockfileVersion 1 records no install scripts: they are known from the registry's manifest only

deps.reason.unproven: {path} is in no layout that names the package and version, so its identity is not proven
deps.reason.heldTooMuch: answers past {mb} MB held at once
deps.reason.fromEnvKey: a key read from the environment
deps.reason.tls: TLS checks of the registry are changed
deps.reason.scriptsDropped: the commit drops the line that keeps install scripts off
deps.reason.bundledUnproven: bundled: the lock cannot prove which version the package holds
deps.unlisted: {path}: {n} new entries come from a source the check cannot prove, and nothing measured them: {where}
deps.git: {path}: {n} new entries are git dependencies, which npm builds by running their prepare script, even with ignore-scripts, and checks no integrity: {where}; listing the exact resolved, pinned to a full commit, in security.deps.sources is for the user to decide
deps.unlistedEntry: {where} comes from a source the check cannot prove: {reason}
deps.gitEntry: {where} is a git dependency, which npm builds by running its prepare script, even with ignore-scripts, and checks no integrity: {reason}; listing the exact resolved, pinned to a full commit, in security.deps.sources is for the user to decide

deps.reason.from: from {from}: listing that registry in security.deps.registries or this exact resolved in security.deps.sources is for the user to decide

deps.reason.outside: {from}: outside the repository: listing this exact resolved in security.deps.sources is for the user to decide

deps.reason.inRepo: a file the repository holds: what it holds is not read

hook.installed: commit-msg hook installed: {path}. Messages written with git commit are checked now (cherry-pick, revert and autosquash folds do not run commit-msg hooks).
hook.wired: {path} already runs commit-check; nothing to do.
hook.notThere: {path} is not there, so git runs no commit-msg hook and nothing is checked: a hook manager writes it when it installs (husky: npm install).
hook.notExecutable: git does not run {path}: it is not executable, so nothing is checked. Make it executable: {chmod}
hook.blockUnread: {own} names commit-check, but it is not the block or the line install-hook prints here, so Ennyn cannot tell whether it runs on every commit. Nothing was written. Put the block below at the top of {own}, before any other command and above husky's own line if it has one, in place of the old call or block.
hook.blockUnreadPlain: {own} names commit-check, but it is not the block or the line install-hook prints here, so Ennyn cannot tell whether it runs on every commit. Nothing was written. Run install-hook from the Claude Code plugin (/ennyn:init, or --plugin-data "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}"): it prints the block that goes at the top of {own}, above husky's own line if it has one. A copy of Ennyn the project keeps itself is called there by its path in the repository; doctor cannot read such a call and keeps warning. A hook on this machine alone (.git/hooks) can hold this line instead, first and as it stands here: {line}
hook.late: {own} may skip commit-check: the index holds a file in husky's stub directory, which git runs before the project's own hook, so a commit can change what runs. Nothing was written. Take it out of the index (git rm --cached) and run husky again.
hook.hooksOff: core.hooksPath is set but empty, so git runs no hook and nothing is checked. Nothing was written. Remove that setting (git config --show-origin core.hooksPath names where it is), then run install-hook again.
hook.blockUnrecorded: {own} holds Ennyn's block, which reads the plugin version from {data}, where none is recorded, so every commit goes through unchecked. Nothing was written: start a Claude Code session with the plugin, which records the version it runs.
hook.blockStale: {own} holds Ennyn's block, which reads the plugin version from {data}, whose record names nothing it may run, so every commit is refused. Nothing was written: start a Claude Code session with the plugin, which records the version it runs.
hook.blockNoNode: {own} holds Ennyn's block, which takes no PATH entry inside this repository, and no node is left on PATH, so every commit goes through unchecked. Nothing was written: put a directory outside the repository that holds node on PATH.
hook.blockNoData: {own} holds Ennyn's block, which finds no plugin data directory it may read here (no HOME, no absolute path, one it cannot enter, or one inside this repository), so every commit is refused. Nothing was written: set HOME, or ENNYN_PLUGIN_DATA to the plugin's data directory.
hook.cliGone: {path} runs {cli}, which is not there, so every commit goes through unchecked. Ennyn writes nothing under core.hooksPath ({dir}); put this line in its place: {line}
hook.other: {path} is another hook; it was not touched. Add this line to it, as its first command, exactly as it stands here: {line}
hook.cliRefused: {path} runs the plugin version recorded in {data}, which is gone, so every commit is refused. Ennyn writes nothing under core.hooksPath ({dir}); put this line in its place: {line}
hook.cliForeign: {path} reads the plugin version from {data}, whose record is no regular file Ennyn wrote (a link, or not a regular file), so every commit is refused. Delete that record, then run install-hook from the plugin (/ennyn:init).
hook.cliPinned: {path} names one plugin version ({cli}), so it stops checking once Claude Code replaces that version. Ennyn writes nothing under core.hooksPath ({dir}); put this line in its place: {line}
hook.cliOtherVersion: {path} reads the record in {data}, which names {recorded}, not this session's version ({root}): installs of the plugin in two scopes share one record, and the session that started last decides. The hook needs no change; start the session whose version should check commits.
hook.followsRecord: {path} follows the plugin through the record in {data} (it names {recorded}); install-hook from this copy ({root}) would turn it into a hook pinned to this copy. Nothing was written. Run install-hook from the plugin (/ennyn:init), pass --plugin-data with that directory to record this copy, or delete the hook to install this copy by its path.
hook.dataInRepository: The plugin's data directory {data} is inside this repository, where its record would be the repository's own file. Nothing was written: give the plugin's own data directory (${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}).
hook.dataName: The plugin's data directory {data} does not end in a name the block can hold (letters, digits, dot, underscore, hyphen). Nothing was written: give the plugin's own data directory (${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}).
hook.cliUnrecorded: {path} reads the plugin version from {data}, where none is recorded, so every commit goes through unchecked. Ennyn writes nothing under core.hooksPath ({dir}); put this line in its place: {line}
hook.replacedCopy: This copy of Ennyn ({root}) is a plugin version Claude Code has replaced and deletes 14 days after; a hook that ran it would then stop checking. Nothing was written: start a new Claude Code session and run install-hook from it.
hook.notRecorded: The plugin version was not recorded and no hook was written: {error}
hook.cliReplaced: {path} runs {root}, a plugin version Claude Code has replaced and deletes 14 days after, so commits are checked by that version's rules. Ennyn writes nothing under core.hooksPath ({dir}); put this line in its place: {line}
hook.follows: The hook runs the plugin version the latest Claude Code session started with (recorded in {data}), so it follows plugin updates.
doctor.filesUnmeasured: tracked files: unmeasured ({error}); the instruction budget, review.cochange and review.forbidden checks need them
doctor.hookMissing: commit-msg hook: none, so these are rules on paper: {rules}; run ennyn install-hook
doctor.hookOther: commit-msg hook: {path} does not run commit-check; ennyn install-hook says what to add
doctor.hookPath: commit-msg hook: core.hooksPath is {dir} and its commit-msg does not run commit-check; ennyn install-hook says what to add
doctor.hookNotRun: commit-msg hook: git does not run {path}: it is not executable, so no commit is checked; run ennyn install-hook
doctor.hookUnread: commit-msg hook: {path} names commit-check, but it is not the block or the line install-hook prints here, so doctor cannot tell whether it runs on every commit; ennyn install-hook prints the block
doctor.hookLate: commit-msg hook: {path} may skip commit-check: the index holds a file in husky's stub directory, which git runs before the project's own hook, so a commit can change what runs; take it out of the index
doctor.hookBlockUnrecorded: commit-msg hook: {path} holds Ennyn's block, which reads the plugin version from {data}, where none is recorded (the plugin is not installed for this user, was uninstalled, or has not run since), so every commit goes through unchecked; a Claude Code session with the plugin records it
doctor.hookBlockStale: commit-msg hook: {path} holds Ennyn's block, which reads the plugin version from {data}, whose record names nothing it may run (gone, no absolute path, no regular file, a CLI that is a link, or a path inside this repository), so every commit is refused; a Claude Code session with the plugin records the version it runs
doctor.hookBlockNoNode: commit-msg hook: {path} holds Ennyn's block, which takes no PATH entry inside this repository, and no node is left on PATH, so every commit goes through unchecked; put a directory outside the repository that holds node on PATH
doctor.hookBlockNoData: commit-msg hook: {path} holds Ennyn's block, which finds no plugin data directory it may read here (no HOME, no absolute path, one it cannot enter, or one inside this repository), so every commit is refused; set HOME, or ENNYN_PLUGIN_DATA to the plugin's data directory
doctor.hookAbsent: commit-msg hook: {path} is not there, so git runs no hook and no commit is checked; ennyn install-hook says why
doctor.hookCliGone: commit-msg hook: {path} runs {cli}, which is not there, so every commit goes through unchecked; run ennyn install-hook again
doctor.hookPluginUnrecorded: commit-msg hook: {path} reads the plugin version from {data}, where none is recorded (the plugin was uninstalled, or has not run since), so every commit goes through unchecked; run ennyn install-hook from the plugin (/ennyn:init), or delete the hook
doctor.hookPluginStale: commit-msg hook: {path} runs the plugin version recorded in {data} ({root}), which names no version it can run (gone, or no absolute path), so every commit is refused; run ennyn install-hook from the plugin (/ennyn:init), or delete the hook if the plugin is uninstalled
doctor.hookRecordForeign: commit-msg hook: {path} reads the plugin version from {record}, which is no record Ennyn wrote (a link, or not a regular file), so every commit is refused; delete {record}, then run ennyn install-hook from the plugin (/ennyn:init)
doctor.hookSelfReplaced: commit-msg hook: {path} checks commits, but this copy of Ennyn ({own}) is a plugin version Claude Code has replaced, so this session runs the old version; start a new Claude Code session
doctor.hookReplaced: commit-msg hook: {path} runs {root}, a plugin version Claude Code has replaced and deletes 14 days after, so commits are checked by that version's rules; run ennyn install-hook from the plugin (/ennyn:init)
doctor.hookPinned: commit-msg hook: {path} names one plugin version ({cli}), so it stops checking once Claude Code replaces that version; run ennyn install-hook from this session to make it follow plugin updates
doctor.hookOtherVersion: commit-msg hook: {path} runs {root}, not this copy of the plugin ({own}): installs of the plugin in two scopes share one record, and the session that started last decides which version checks commits
pluginRoot.notRecorded: ennyn: the plugin version this session runs could not be applied to the commit-msg hook's record, so the hook may run another version ({error}).
hook.hooksPath.repo: core.hooksPath is {dir}, a directory in the repository and usually tracked; this machine's path does not belong there, so nothing was written. Run install-hook from the Claude Code plugin (/ennyn:init, or --plugin-data "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}"): it prints a block for {dir}/commit-msg that finds the plugin on each machine. A copy of Ennyn the project keeps itself is called from there by its path in the repository; doctor cannot read such a call and keeps warning.
hook.hooksPath.husky: husky runs the hooks ({dir} holds its generated stubs), so nothing was written. Run install-hook from the Claude Code plugin (/ennyn:init, or --plugin-data "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}"): it prints a block for {own} that finds the plugin on each machine. A copy of Ennyn the project keeps itself is called from there by its path in the repository; doctor cannot read such a call and keeps warning.
hook.hooksPath.repoBlock: core.hooksPath is {dir}, a directory in the repository and usually tracked, so Ennyn writes nothing there. Paste the block below at the top of {dir}/commit-msg, before any other command (husky 6 to 8: above its husky.sh line, where it runs twice, harmlessly; a new file starts with #!/bin/sh and must be executable). There it checks every commit the hook sees: an early exit of the project's own (an exempt subject, a marker) skips only the project's checks; under husky, HUSKY=0 skips the whole hook, as --no-verify does. It names no path of this machine: it finds the plugin's data directory from the Claude Code session (ENNYN_PLUGIN_DATA), CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR or HOME, and the plugin version from the record there.
hook.hooksPath.huskyBlock: husky runs the hooks ({dir} holds its generated stubs), so Ennyn writes nothing there. Paste the block below at the top of {own}, before any other command and above husky's own line if it has one. There it checks every commit the hook sees: an early exit of the project's own (an exempt subject, a marker) skips only the project's checks; HUSKY=0 skips the whole hook, as --no-verify does. It names no path of this machine: it finds the plugin's data directory from the Claude Code session (ENNYN_PLUGIN_DATA), CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR or HOME, and the plugin version from the record there.
hook.hooksPath.global: core.hooksPath is {dir}, outside this repository: it applies to every repository on this machine. To check them all, add this line to {dir}/commit-msg, as its first command, exactly as it stands here: {line}
cli.hookConfigBroken: ennyn: the config does not load, so this commit was not checked: not its message, not its lines ({error}). Fix it, in this commit if you like.
cli.hookMessageUnreadable: ennyn: {path} could not be read ({error}), so this commit was not checked.
cli.hookConfigRefused: ennyn: commit refused: {path} is there and could not be read ({error}), so no check can run. No commit holds that file, so no commit can fix it: repair or remove it; ennyn doctor says why.
cli.hookConfigUnread: ennyn: git failed ({git}) before the commit's own config was read, and the work tree's does not load ({error}), so this commit was not checked: not its message, not its lines.
cli.hookGitFailed: ennyn: git failed ({error}), so this commit was not checked: not its message, not its lines.
cli.hookConfigAbsent: ennyn: ENNYN_CONFIG names {path}, which is not there, and no commit holds a config, so this commit was not checked; the defaults are not this project's rules.
cli.hookElsewhere: ennyn: commit refused: git is committing from a place that is not this repository's own top (a work tree apart from its git dir: --work-tree, GIT_WORK_TREE, core.worktree, GIT_DIR from a subdirectory, or a hook that changed folder before this check), so the checks cannot read this commit. Commit from the repository's top with none of them set, and run this check first in a project's hook. A bare repository with a work tree of its own cannot be checked.
cli.hookWhereUntold: ennyn: commit refused: could not tell where git is committing ({error}), so the checks cannot read this commit. Commit from the repository's top once git answers there.
cli.hookMessageUnchecked: ennyn: this commit's message was not checked, nor its review.forbidden lines ({error}); security.ci, security.deps and security.secrets ran.
cli.secretsProbeFailed: Whether this is a repository could not be read ({error}); the secret scan went on.

doctor.askOk: ask rules: .claude/settings.json, as committed, holds {rules}. Claude Code applies them only in a session started at the repository's top (one started in a subdirectory reads that directory's .claude/), not when any setting in the file is one it rejects (it skips the file whole and shows a Settings Error), and not in a cloud project thread or a session over several repositories; a command written another way is not matched: a git option before push (git -C <dir> push, git -c k=v push), a quoted or escaped push (git "push"), a command fed to a shell or another program (sh -c, eval, xargs, find -exec), a command word built as it runs ($(…), `…`), an alias, a script that pushes, gh api, an MCP tool, and on older versions a full path (before 2.1.309) or a subshell (2.1.207)

doctor.askUncommitted: ask rules: .claude/settings.json holds {rules}, but not as committed (the file is untracked, ignored or changed), so other clones do not have them; commit the file
doctor.askLocal: ask rules: only .claude/settings.local.json holds {rules}, so only this machine has them
doctor.askUnread: ask rules: unmeasured: {list} gives no rule (not a JSON object, over 2 MB, hooks or permissions in a shape Claude Code rejects, or a link out of the repository)

doctor.worktreesNotIgnored: agent worktrees: git does not ignore {path}, where Claude Code puts agent worktrees: git status lists them, git add -A commits each as an embedded repository, and a tool run over . reads their unfinished code; add {path} to .gitignore and commit it (/ennyn:init proposes the line)
doctor.worktreesNegated: agent worktrees: {source}:{line} ({pattern}) un-ignores what Claude Code puts in {path}: git status lists it, git add -A commits each worktree as an embedded repository, and a tool run over . reads their unfinished code; change that line, or add {path} after it, and commit it

doctor.worktreesUnmeasured: agent worktrees: whether git ignores {path} is unmeasured: {error}
